title: `substring` raises for an offset or a length outside 32 bits
description: DuckDB's `substring(s, start, length)` raises "Substring offset outside of supported range" for a `start` outside `[-2³², 2³²)`, and "Substring length outside of supported range" for a `length` of `2³²` or more. With a NULL string, offset or length it gives NULL.
reference: Was: no such error; `Rel.eval` returned rows, and `verify` reported nothing (#336).

Now: the same range is an error in the reference (`Text.substrInRange`, `Issue.domain`), reported by `verify` unless the offset's bounds rule it out. The size hypothesis for strings is 2³² characters (`Text.sizeCap`). DuckDB raises itself; the written plan guards the offset its wrap-around arithmetic shifts.
